title: Section 5: Daily Care, Home Safety & Caregiver Support
source_document: English Master Data Collection & Clinical Content Repository

items: Pressure Relief Awareness: Regular weight shifts and repositioning help prevent skin breakdown. Specific positioning methods and schedules should be determined by a qualified healthcare professional.

Skin Inspection Awareness: Educational resources highlight the importance of routine skin monitoring (such as morning and evening checks with mirrors or caregiver assistance) to identify early skin changes over high-risk bony prominences (sacrum, ischial tuberosities, trochanters, heels, scapulae).
Moisture Management: Maintain clean, dry skin; address urinary/fecal incontinence immediately; avoid harsh soaps and vigorous friction rubbing.

rows: Gradual inclines (such as a 1:12 slope guideline) facilitate safer manual and powered wheelchair propulsion.
Sufficient clear door opening width (typically 32 to 36 inches) allows comfortable wheelchair clearance.
Roll-in showers with flat thresholds, wall-mounted grab bars (rated for weight bearing), elevated toilet seats, padded shower chairs.
Complete removal of throw rugs, exposed electrical cords, and uneven thresholds. Adequate illumination along all transit corridors.

items: Bladder Management: Bladder care routines must be prescribed, evaluated, and monitored by a qualified healthcare professional or urologist based on individual clinical evaluation.
Bowel Management: Bowel management plans require clinical assessment and guidance from healthcare specialists based on individual neurogenic bowel conditions.
Respiratory support techniques and devices must be evaluated, prescribed, and monitored by qualified healthcare professionals.
Active connection with peer-mentorship networks, specialized disability sports associations, and vocational rehabilitation programs to facilitate community re-entry and long-term adaptation.
Ergonomics & Assistance: Caregivers should receive hands-on training from healthcare professionals regarding proper body mechanics and assistive techniques to protect safety and wellbeing.

Respite & Support: Caregivers play a vital role in supporting independence. Incorporating ergonomic transfer techniques, respectful encouragement, stress management, and professional respite care helps prevent caregiver burnout and maintains long-term wellbeing.
